caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 97 of 2011
lawyer:
Md. Shohrowardi, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent
parties:
The State ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Mostafa Kamal alias Ruman ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Muhammad Inman Ali J. This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 10.02.2011 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4624 of 2009 making the Rule absolute thereby confirming the order of ad-interim bail granted earlier. 

 2. Facts of the case relevant for disposal of the instant petition are that Md. Kanchan Hossen as informant lodged a First Information Report (FIR) on 06.10.2008 at about 19.05 hours with Rupgonj Police Station alleging, inter aim, that his son Hasib Hossen alias Prince, a student of Jagannath University, left his house by motorcycle on 4.10.2008 and informed him on 05.10.2008 on his mobile phone that he was in Narayanganj with a friend and would return home after spending the night with his friend. But since morning of 06.10.2008 he could not contact his son on his mobile phone as it was switched of. At about 1.30 p.m. he received information over the telephone from Rupgonj Police Station that an unknown dead body of a man was laying near Ahmadia Rolling Industry. At 2.00 p.m. he along with his wife and daughter went there and identified the dead of his son. He further stated in the FIR that he suspected that at some time before 12.10 hours on 05.10.2008 his friends in a preplanned manner murdered him and left him at that place. He also stated that his son had cut injuries inflicted with a sharp knife on his head, chest, belly and back. 

 4. While the matter was pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate the accused-respondent prayed for bail which was rejected. A prayer for bail moved before the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj was also rejected in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 400 of 2009 arising out of G.R. No. 507/2008 corresponding to Rupgonj Police Station Case No. 4(10)2008 dated 06.10.2008 under sections 302/201/34 of the Penal Code. 

 5. Against the order of rejection of hail the accused respondent filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4624 of 2009 before the High Court Division where-upon Rule was issued and an order passed granting ad-interim bail on 23.03.2009 for a period of 3 (three) months, which was thereafter extended from time to time. 

 7. Mr. Md. Shohrowardi, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that inculpatory confessional statement by co-accused disclosed the name of the accused respondent mentioning his active participation in the killing of the victim. He further submits that the case is under investigation and that the judgment and order granting bail to the accused respondent will frustrate the purpose of the prosecution case creating obstacle in the way of fair/free investigation. 

 10. Grant on bail in any case is at the discretion of the Court considering the matter. In the instant case it appears from the impugned judgment of the High Cowl Division that the High Court Division noted that except the confession of co-accused there is no other incriminating materials to connect the accused with the alleged occurrence. Moreover, the ad-interim bail was granted on 23.03.2009 and till the date of judgment of the Court Division on 10.02.2011 there was no allegation before the Court that the accused had misused the privilege of bail in any way whatsoever. Accordingly, the Rule was made absolute. 

 11. We are of the view that the High Court Division properly exercised its discretion in the facts and circumstances of the case and we do not find any reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.
